sections.html:
Moon Township sits on the south bank of the Ohio River in western Allegheny County. The 2020 census counted 27,261 residents, and the July 2025 estimate is 26,756, a slip of 1.8 percent after 12.7 percent growth in the 2010s. The ZIP code is 15108. Workers spend about 28.2 minutes getting to their jobs on average.

A separate Moon Township exists in Beaver County, so confirm Allegheny County when you search property records. Crescent Township and Coraopolis lie to the north, Findlay and North Fayette townships to the west and south, and Robinson Township to the east. The Moon Area School District serves the township, and Crescent Township sits in that district too, which helps when you compare nearby addresses.

Pittsburgh International Airport opened in Moon in 1951, with Parkway West, I-376 and I-79 exits nearby. The passenger terminal moved to neighboring Findlay Township in 1991, but a large share of the runways and the cargo area remain inside the township. Robert Morris University has its main campus here, and University Boulevard is the business corridor. The 911th Airlift Wing, the 171st Air Refueling Wing and the National Weather Service forecast office are also based in the township.

Houses close to University Boulevard or the airport face different noise and traffic than those on quiet interior streets, and buyers will ask which kind yours is.

Owners occupy 78.1 percent of Moon's homes, so most listings compete with other owner-occupied houses rather than rentals. Median owners with a mortgage pay $2,208 a month, a number that helps you gauge what a buyer can afford.

Moon's winters hover around the freezing line and moisture arrives in every season, with about 41.80 inches of precipitation a year. A hillside lot has to shed that water, and buyers and inspectors look for signs of trouble. Before you list, check:

  • Roof condition and gutters, since water has to move off a hillside lot
  • Basement dampness and sump pump history
  • Retaining walls, steps and driveway surfaces that heave in winter
  • Furnace age and the efficiency of the heating system

Receipts for roof or drainage work give you something concrete to show.

Moon requires a rental inspection before each change of occupants. The township's rental packet asks for an inspection request form, an affidavit, an inspection agreement and a rental registration, with a $20 fee per unit. The Fire Marshal's office then schedules the appointment, and owners must report the names of all occupants within 30 days of move-in. An investor buying to rent would go through the same steps.

If you are selling a house with a tenant, a buyer who keeps that tenant should check that the paperwork is on file.

Mooncrest was built in 1943 as housing for defense workers, and its homes were sold to private investors in the mid-1950s. A property there needs a Certificate of Appropriateness before the township will issue a building permit. The township's Mooncrest Historic Overlay Advisory Committee advises the Board of Supervisors on those certificates.

Building permits are required for alterations, additions, porch roofs and sheds, and rules cover windows and doors along building fronts, dryer vents, coal chutes and roofing materials. Call the township office at 412-262-1700 to ask whether an address falls inside the district, and hand a buyer the permit and inspection records.

Moon charges one-half percent for the township and one-half percent for the Moon Area School District. With the state's 1 percent, a sale carries 2 percent in transfer tax. You pay it at recording by its own check, apart from recording fees. Family transfers can be exempt, and deeds that show no price need a Statement of Value.

An owner who disputes an assessment can go to the county's BPAAR board, whose hearings are held by phone. Gather recent sales of similar Moon houses and photos of any condition problems before the hearing, and ask the county for the current filing window. A lower assessment lowers your bill while you hold the house, though it does not change what a buyer will pay.

Speed comes down to inspection readiness and whether the buyer needs a lender. Moon owners usually compare three routes:

  • List on the open market and wait for a buyer who will live there, the route that can bring the top price for a house in good shape.
  • Sell as is to a cash buyer, a fit for estates, tenant-occupied houses and properties needing repairs.
  • Sell to a neighbor, a relative or an investor you already know.

A house in the Mooncrest district or with a rental history should come with its permits and inspection records, since buyers will ask.

sections.h2: What happens after you accept an offer
sections.html:
With a cash buyer the path is short. You agree on a price and a closing date, the title company searches the deed for liens, and you gather your mortgage payoff if you owe one. No lender appraisal or underwriting stands between signing and closing. At the table you sign the deed, the 2 percent transfer tax is paid with its own check, and the title company sends you whatever remains after payoffs.

With a listing, the same steps follow a buyer's loan approval and appraisal, which adds weeks and gives a buyer room to renegotiate if the house falls short. If your Moon house is a rental, finish the inspection and registration before the sale so the buyer inherits clean paperwork.

sections.h2: Paperwork to line up before you list
sections.html:
Start with the basics a title company will ask for: the deed, your mortgage lender's name and any lien or tax notice. Then make a short list of anything done to the house that needed a permit, such as an addition, porch roof or shed, and find the paperwork. In the Mooncrest district, add the Certificate of Appropriateness for exterior work.

Next, decide how you want to be paid and how fast. Estates and tenant-occupied houses often suit a cash buyer, while a house in good shape may earn more on the open market. Whichever you pick, ask the township office at 412-262-1700 about open inspections or registrations so nothing surprises you after you accept an offer.

faqs.q: Is Moon Township the same as Moon, Pennsylvania?
faqs.a: Yes. Moon Township is in Allegheny County and is the place most people mean. A separate Moon Township exists in Beaver County, so confirm the county when you search property records.

faqs.q: What is the transfer tax on a house sale in Moon Township?
faqs.a: Two percent altogether: 1 percent to the state, one-half percent to Moon Township and one-half percent to the Moon Area School District.

faqs.q: Do I need a rental inspection to sell a Moon house with a tenant?
faqs.a: Moon inspects a rental before each new occupant, charging $20 a unit, and wants a rental registration within 30 days of move-in. A buyer keeping the tenant should check that the paperwork is on file.

faqs.q: What is the Mooncrest Historic District?
faqs.a: It is a historic overlay area built in 1943 as defense worker housing. A Certificate of Appropriateness must come before any building permit there, with an advisory committee making recommendations to the supervisors.

faqs.q: Which school district serves Moon Township?
faqs.a: The Moon Area School District. Crescent Township also sits in that district, which helps when comparing nearby addresses.
